title: Design an RDS Deployment
description: Plan a highly available, secure RDS setup for a web app.
problemStatement:
Your team is deploying a customer‑facing web application on EC2 instances. The backend uses a PostgreSQL database. Design an RDS deployment that meets these requirements:
- The database must survive an Availability Zone failure automatically.
- Read‑heavy workloads must be offloaded to improve performance.
- Data must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
- You need point‑in‑time recovery for the last 14 days.
- The database must not be accessible from the internet.

Describe:
- The RDS instance engine and configuration (Multi‑AZ, Read Replicas).
- Security group settings.
- Backup and encryption settings.
- How the application servers will connect.
hints: Multi‑AZ for high availability, Read Replicas for read scaling.
Security groups: only allow inbound from the app servers’ security group on port 5432 (PostgreSQL).
Enable encryption at creation; use SSL for connections.
solutionCode:
Engine: PostgreSQL (latest supported version).
Instance class: db.r5.large (or appropriate size).
Multi‑AZ: Enabled – synchronous standby in another AZ for automatic failover.
Read Replica: One Read Replica in the same region (can be in another AZ) to handle reporting queries; the application directs read‑only operations to the replica endpoint.

Security:
- Place the RDS instance in private subnets (no public IP).
- Security group `sg‑rds` allows inbound TCP 5432 from `sg‑web‑app` (the application servers’ security group). No inbound from 0.0.0.0/0.
- Enable SSL for database connections; the application uses the RDS CA certificate.

Encryption: Enable encryption at creation with a KMS key. This encrypts storage, backups, snapshots, and replicas.

Backup: Enable automated backups with 14‑day retention, allowing point‑in‑time recovery to any 5‑minute window. Take manual snapshots before major changes.

Connection: The application uses the RDS endpoint (DNS name), which resolves to the primary instance. For reads, it uses the Read Replica endpoint.
